scope: git diff main..002-cli-tool: fairdm_docs/cli.py, fairdm_docs/config.py, tests/conftest.py, tests/test_cli.py, tests/test_config.py, tests/fixtures/**, docs/adr/0009 + 0010, docs/adr/index.md, README.md, CHANGELOG.md, pyproject.toml, and specs/002-cli-tool/{spec.md,decisions.md} against ADR 0009/0010 and the code's actual behaviour.

findings.claim: The redirect classifier in `check()` only recognises a 302 redirect. A 301, 307 or 308 redirect matches neither the broken branch nor the redirected branch, so it silently vanishes from both the console output and check-report.txt — never reported as broken, never reported as redirected, contradicting FR-013 and ADR 0009's stated fix for exactly this failure mode.
findings.evidence: fairdm_docs/cli.py:265-268 classifies with `if ": [broken]" in line: ... elif ": [redirected with " in line:`. Sphinx's own linkcheck (sphinx/builders/linkcheck.py:174-199, write_entry at :213-216) writes the bracket text as `redirected permanently` for 301/308, `redirected with Found` for 302, `redirected with See Other` for 303, `redirected temporarily` for 307, and `redirected with unknown code` otherwise — i.e. `f'[{what}]'` where `what` is `f'redirected {text}'`. Only the two `with `-prefixed variants (302, 303, and the fallback) contain the substring `: [redirected with `; `redirected permanently` and `redirected temporarily` do not. Verified directly: `": [redirected with " in "index.rst:5: [redirected permanently] http://example.com to http://example.com/"` evaluates to `False`. Every fixture and test in this diff (tests/conftest.py's `_RedirectHandler`, tests/test_cli.py's `_TerminatingRedirectHandler`) sends `self.send_response(302)`, so the gap has no test coverage and was not caught. decisions.md's D5 record describes the original bug as a literal-string mismatch (`": [redirected]"` vs `"[redirected with Found]"`) and presents the fix as complete; it does not mention that Sphinx's bracket text varies by HTTP status code, so the fix only covers the 302/303 cases the record's own reproduction used.
findings.reproduction: Point a documentation source at an address that returns a 301 (or 307/308) redirect and run `fairdm-docs check`. The address is absent from both the console's redirect list and check-report.txt, and the command still exits 0 — the address is neither confirmed working nor flagged, it simply disappears from the report.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the `with ` from the match so it covers all four bracket texts Sphinx emits, e.g. `elif ": [redirected " in line:` (every variant begins `redirected ` followed by descriptive text, so this still excludes `: [broken]` and any other status).

findings.claim: README.md's new "Exit Codes" section still states the live preview server's Ctrl+C exits 0, but the code in this same diff fixes that to exit 130 (D6/ADR 0010). The caveat is now false and contradicts the command's actual, tested behaviour.
findings.evidence: README.md's Exit Codes section (added this diff) reads: "130 - Interrupted with Ctrl+C, for a plain build or a check. The live preview server's Ctrl+C currently exits 0 instead." fairdm_docs/cli.py:141-143 raises `typer.Exit(code=130)` on `KeyboardInterrupt` in the live-preview branch, and tests/test_cli.py:1223-1238 (`test_live_preview_interrupted_exits_130`) asserts `result.exit_code == 130` and passes. decisions.md D14's own implementation note anticipated this exact drift: "Revisit if: the story that implements D6 lands — the caveat sentence should come out of the README in that same change" — D6 has landed in this diff (D6's own decisions.md entry says "Settled: 130 everywhere"), but the README sentence was not removed.
findings.reproduction: Read README.md's Exit Codes section as shipped in this diff, then run `fairdm-docs build --live` and press Ctrl+C: the command exits 130, not 0 as the README states.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the trailing sentence "The live preview server's Ctrl+C currently exits 0 instead." and fold live preview into the general 130 claim, per D14's own revisit note.
